name: 5-Amino-1MQ
route: Mostly capsules from unregulated sellers; no approved form
status: Not FDA-approved and not a peptide. Studied only in cells and mice; no human studies found
mechanism: Blocks NNMT, an enzyme in fat tissue, which in mice raised NAD+ and cellular energy use and reduced diet-induced obesity

article.summary: 5-Amino-1MQ is a small molecule, not a peptide, sold online as a fat-loss and metabolism booster. It blocks an enzyme called NNMT in mice, but no human studies exist and it is not FDA-approved.
article.takeaway: 5-Amino-1MQ (5-amino-1-methylquinolinium) is often marketed alongside peptides, but it is a small synthetic molecule that blocks an enzyme called NNMT. NNMT is overactive in the fat tissue of obese mice, and lowering it protected mice from diet-induced obesity in a 2014 Nature study.[^1] NNMT-blocking small molecules reversed high-fat-diet obesity in mice in 2018,[^2] and 5-amino-1MQ itself, paired with a low-fat diet, produced rapid fat loss in obese mice.[^3] No human studies were found, so whether it helps, harms or does nothing in people is unknown. It is not FDA-approved.
glance: Not approved; no approved medical use
Fat loss, higher NAD+ and metabolism (unproven in people)
Small-molecule NNMT inhibitor, not a peptide
Falls under WADA's non-approved substances rule (S0), banned at all times

blocks.text: NNMT (nicotinamide N-methyltransferase) is an enzyme that uses up nicotinamide, a form of vitamin B3 that cells need to make NAD+, a molecule central to energy metabolism. NNMT activity is higher in the fat tissue and liver of obese and diabetic mice. Turning NNMT down in mice raised NAD+ and energy expenditure and protected against diet-induced obesity.[^1]

5-Amino-1MQ is a small, cell-permeable molecule that inhibits NNMT. The idea is that a pill could imitate what genetic knockdown does in mice, helping fat cells burn more energy.[^2] Marketing often lumps it with peptides, but it is not one.

rows: Lowering NNMT in fat and liver protected against diet-induced obesity by raising energy expenditure[^1]
Membrane-permeable small molecules reversed high-fat-diet obesity[^2]
With a switch to a low-fat diet, rapid loss of body fat in obese mice, and a distinct gut microbiome[^3]
No clinical studies found in PubMed or ClinicalTrials.gov as of October 2026

blocks.text: Findings in mice rarely carry over to people. A 2026 review noted that NNMT inhibitors have faced low target engagement, poor bioavailability and unknown safety profiles, although newer compounds look more promising.[^4]

items: **No human safety data:** doses, side effects, interactions and long-term effects in people have not been reported
**A widely used enzyme:** NNMT also works in the liver and other tissues and is tied to methylation and nicotinamide metabolism, so effects beyond fat cells are plausible but unmeasured in people[^1]
**Gray-market quality:** products sold as supplements or research chemicals are not made to drug standards, so identity, purity and amount are unverified
**Unstudied groups:** pregnancy, children, people with diabetes or liver disease, and long-term use

blocks.text: 5-Amino-1MQ is not an FDA-approved drug and has no approved medical use. Sellers often label it for research, but products promoted for use in people are unapproved drugs.

The World Anti-Doping Agency's S0 class prohibits, at all times, any pharmacological substance without government approval for human therapeutic use, including drugs in pre-clinical development. 5-Amino-1MQ is not named on the 2026 list, but it would fall under that rule.

5-Amino-1MQ is a mouse-stage idea sold as if it were proven. The biology of NNMT is real, and researchers are working toward clinical development of NNMT inhibitors,[^4] but this compound has no human data and no regulatory standing. For weight or metabolic health, options backed by large randomized trials, such as [semaglutide](/peptides/semaglutide) and [tirzepatide](/peptides/tirzepatide), can be discussed with a clinician.

evidence.label: Very low: mouse studies only
evidence.text: The strongest data are 2014-2022 mouse experiments.[^1][^2][^3] No human study of 5-amino-1MQ was found, and a 2026 review describes the safety profiles of NNMT inhibitors as unknown.[^4]

faq.a: No. It is a small synthetic molecule, a methylated quinolinium compound, that is often sold alongside peptides.[^3]
That is unknown. In obese mice it reduced body fat, especially together with a diet change,[^2][^3] but no human studies have been reported.

faq.a: It has no approval for human use, and products sold for that purpose are unapproved. In sport, WADA's S0 rule bans non-approved substances at all times, which would cover it.
